title: DATEDIF: days, months or years between

screens.prompt: The dates in B and C are serials, not text: put the complete years Ada has served into D2, counting only full years.

hints.func-datedif: Subtracting the two serials gives 790 days; the Y unit is what turns that into complete years.
hints.require-ref: Point at B2 and C2, so the second employee needs no new formula.
hints.value: 1 January 2022 to 1 March 2024 is 2 whole years. The two months after that anniversary do not count.
hints.error: The unit has to be one of Y, M, D, YM, MD or YD; anything else returns #NUM!.

screens.prompt: Same person, different question: put the complete months since Grace started into D2.

hints.syntax: The same three arguments with the month unit: =DATEDIF(B2,C2,"M").
hints.func-datedif: M counts complete months, not days divided by thirty.
hints.require-ref: Read Grace's start and the review date from B2 and C2.
hints.value: 1 January 2021 to 1 March 2024 is 38 whole months: 36 for the three years, then two more.
hints.error: A reversed pair returns #NUM!, so if the number is an error check the dates before the quotes.

docs.explain:
Subtracting one date from another answers in days and nothing else. DATEDIF takes a start date, an end date and a unit in quotes, and answers in whichever unit you name. Y, M and D give whole units; YM, MD and YD give what is left after the whole ones.

Ada started on 1 January 2022 and the review is 1 March 2024, so the Y answer is 2. A subtraction on that pair gives 790 and M gives 26, both correct answers to other questions. The second screen asks for Grace's complete months and expects 38.

Nothing in the call checks that the unit matches the question, so a wrong one returns a plausible number. Excel leaves DATEDIF out of its function list, so type the name in full. A start date after the end returns #NUM! instead of a negative count.

errors.text: The end date falls before the start date, so there is no positive interval for DATEDIF to report.
The unit in quotes is not Y, M, D, YM, MD or YD, so there is no unit to count.
One of the dates is text that Excel cannot read as a date, so there is no serial to compare.

docs.atWork: A staff review sheet reporting complete years of service, without dividing a day count by 365.
docs.outcome: Ask for the gap between two dates in whole years, months or days, with the leftovers when needed.
docs.dataset: Two employees, their start dates and one review date

seo.title: DATEDIF in Excel: days, months or years
seo.description: DATEDIF answers in the unit you name, leftovers included, so Y gives complete years and YM the months after them. A wrong unit returns a plausible number.
